theorem: For fixed J,tau>0 and finite B,K, open XY with L=N+1, gamma=kappa/L, beta=tau L^2, lambda in [-B,B], kappa in [-K,K], the normalized N-chain Gibbs states on the parameter-independent infinite-Fock embedding converge uniformly in full Schatten-1 norm to the normal quasi-free state of h=[[D-tau lambda,K],[-K,-D+tau lambda]], D=2 tau J(-partial_x^2) Dirichlet, K=-4 tau J kappa partial_x. A uniform occupation tail is T_M=4 pi^2 K^2/M+sum_{k>M}exp(-2 tau J k^2) for M>=k0-1, k0=max(1,ceil sqrt(B/(4J))).
proof_evidence: Full residual split, exact column norm, self-adjoint common-core/strong-resolvent convergence, finite covariance/Wick convergence, and gentle high-mode projection in outputs/research/sol_xy_critical/proof.txt §§1-5. outputs/research/sol_xy_critical/checks.py/json: 18 direct spin-vs-BdG cases N=1..6; 62 kernel/column-norm cases L=3..64; 36 residual-tail cases; finite Galerkin block convergence. Exact symbolic N=2 witness in leaf-01 ANISOTROPY_ADDENDUM.txt. Finite checks do not validate the infinite theorem.

baseline_falsifier: Exact finite XY diagonalization is the equal-information baseline. Failure of the residual tail, common-core resolvent convergence, or fixed covariance-block convergence would falsify the theorem. This is a whole-experiment result for one free-fermion path model, not every local critical lattice.

This establishes an upper bound only.

Under Weyl scaling omega_k~k^(z/d), R_k=O(k^(2r/d)), this sufficient criterion is 2(z-r)>d. Independent BCS pair blocks show sharp failure of vacuum-Fock trace-norm Cauchy convergence at 2(z-r)<=d.
